recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS BUILDING IS COMPRISED OF A 1ST FLOOR FRONT FURNITURE SALES SHOWROOM WITH AN APARTMENT ABOVE (3135 W. 25 ST. PORTION). THIS FURNITURE WAREHOUSE HAS A FIRE WALL BREACH INTO THE 3 STORY FURNITURE WAREHOUSE PORTION (3137 W. 25 ST.). BOTH 3135 AND 3137 SHARE A COMMON BASEMENT. THIS PROPERTY IS CONSIDERED TO BE A COMMON ADDRESS OF 3135-3137 W. 25 ST. THE 1ST FLOOR OF 3137 HAS BEEN ALTERED INTO AN ONGOING LIVE MUSIC EVENT SPACE WITH A FULLY STOCKED BAR, A MUSIC STAGE, FIXED SEATING AND A LARGE DANCE FLOOR. TICKETS ARE SOLD; ALCOHOL AND FOOD ARE SERVED / SOLD. THERE ARE NO LICENSES FOR EITHER THE FURNITURE STORE / WAREHOUSE OPERATIONS OR THE ILLEGAL EVENT SPACE. THERE ARE NO PLANS, PERMITS OR PPA LICENSE APPLICATIONS ON FILE. ALSO, THERE HAVE BEEN 2 BASEMENT APARTMENTS INSTALLED WITHOUT PLANS / PERMITS. PARTIONS WALLS FORMING ROOMS HAVE BEEN INTALLED AS WELL AS ELECTRICAL AND PLUMBING FIXTURES INSTALLED. BOTH BASEMENT APARTMENTS WERE VACATED AT THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION AS WELL AS THE 1ST FLOOR EVENT CANCELLED.ALSO, A ROOM ON THE 2CD FLOOR OF THE 3137 FURNITURE WAREHOUSE HAS BEEN ALTERED INTO A SMALLER (UNLICENSED) EVENT SPACE. A FULLY STOCKED BAR EXISTS WITH LOUNGE TYPE SEATING. THIS SPAACE WAS VACATED ON THE NIGHT OF THIS INSPECTION AS WELL.THERE WAS NO ENTRY TO THE (3135) 2CD FLOOR APARTMENT. IT APPEARED TO BE VACANT.BASED ON THE EXTENSIVE UNLICENSED ACTIVITY AND THE NUMEROUS  DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS ITEMS THE ENTIRE BUILDING IS TO BE INCLUDED IN THE DOB VACATE ORDER. SECTION 14A4-401.1.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. recent_violations.inspector_comments: THE BASEMENT OF THIS RAT INFESTED APARTMENT BUILDING WHERE THERE IS ONGOING RAT BREEDINDG / STORAGE OF DEAD RATS IS 80% FULL OF JUNK / DEBRIS / GARBAGE. A LICENCED, PROFESSIONAL SERVICE IS TO BE HIRED TO CLEAN OUT OF THIS BASEMENT. THIS IS ABSOLUTELY REQUIRED. THIS MUST INCLUDE A 100% REMOVAL OF ALL OF THE JUNK / DEBRIS / GARBAGE SO AS TO FACILITATE THE PROFESSIONAL CLEANING TO OCCUR. THE CURRENT BASEMENT CONDITION IS DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS IN SO FAR AS THE ENORMOUS AMOUNT OF DEBRIS (EXTREME FIRE HAZARD) AND THE UNSANITARY CONDITION).

recent_violations.ordinance: Failed to remove obstruction from exitway that hampers travel and evacuation.  (13-160-070, 13-196-080)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: SEVERAL TENANTS HAVE PADLOCKED REAR DOORS AT THEIR APARTMENTS. ALSO; 2 OF THE 3 ENCLOSED REAR STAIRWELLS HAVE FURNITURE AND STORED ITEMS COMPLETELY OBSTRUCTING EGRESS. THE GANGWAY GATE AT THE REAR IS LOCKED AS WELL PREVENTING ANY REAR EGRESS, AT GRADE, TO THE PUBLIC WAY. THE FRONT ENTRY GATE AT THE WEST  ELEVATION IS DOUBLE KEY LOCKED. THIS CONDITION PREVENTS ANY TENANT TO GET FAR ENOUGH AWAY FROM THE BUILDING TO ENSURE SAFETY ... DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS.

recent_violations.ordinance: Failed to provide and maintain adequate illumination for public hall and stairwell.  (13-196-080, 13-196-450, 13-160-660, 13-160-670)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THE EMERGENCY LIGHTS ARE INOPERABLE AS WELL AS SEVERAL STAIRWELL LIGHT FIXTURES DESIGNED TO BE ILLUMINATED AFTER SUNSET (THE FRONT AND REAR STAIRWELLS ARE TOO DARK TO SAFELY EGRESS THE BUILDING). DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS).

recent_violations.ordinance: Rid premises of rodents and seal rodent holes. (13-196-530 D, 13-196-540 A, 13-196-630 C)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: IN THE BASEMENT THE OWNER'S SON HAD BEEN STORING RATS IN A LARGE FREEZER IN THIS BASEMENT. 7 OF THE 9 APARTMENT TENANTS TESTIFIED TO THIS LONG TERM, ONGOING COLLECTING OF RATS. THE TENANTS STATED THAT THE BREEDING OF RATS HAS OCCURED AS WELL (NUMEROUS TIMES) AS WELL AS THE CAPTURE OF LIVE RATS FOR KILLING AND FREEZING ... ALL OF WHICH IS A CONCERTED EFFORT TO AQUIRE RODENTS TO FEED THIS PERSONS PET SNAKE. AT THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION AT LEAST 200 DEAD RATS WERE REMOVED FROM THE BROKEN FREEZER IN THE  BASEMENT (THE BASEMENT FREEZER STORING THE RATS HAD MALFUNCTIONED. THE DEAD RATS THAWED OUT AT THAT POINT). THE BUILDING ITSELF IS COMPLETELY INFESTED WITH LIVE RATS. THE STENCH FROM THE DEAD RATS IS AT HORIFFIC PROPORTIONS. THE STENCH PERMEATES EVERY SQUARE FOOT OF THIS BUILDING. THIS IS STILL AN EXTREME HEATH HAZARD DUE TO THE AMOUNT OF DEAD RATS THAT REMAIN IN AREAS IMPOSSIBLE TO EASILY ACCESS. UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES WILL OWNERSHIP OF THIS PROPERTY BE ALLOWED TO DO ANY CLEANING OF THIS BASEMENT. OWNERSHIP IS ABSOLUTELY REQUIRED TO HIRE A PROFESSIONAL EXTERMINATOR. ONLY A SIGNED CONTRACT FOR ONGOING EXTERMINATION WILL CONSIDERED. THIS EXTERMINATION CAN ONLY BEGIN AFTER THE BASEMENT DEBRIS IS REMOVED AND THE BASEMENT IS SANITIZED BY A LICENCED, PROFESSIONAL SERVICE. DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS.

In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
recent_violations.inspector_comments: 1ST FLOOR UNIT,MISSING CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR.
